newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up, but pares gains on ACPC news.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up, but pares gains on ACPC news.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures posted moderate gains on Thursday, but a late round of speculative selling amid news that more coffee would be finding its way to the market knocked prices off session highs, dealers said.

Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) president Rubens Barbosa of Brazil said Thursday that the cartel had agreed at a technical meeting to release an additional 200,000 bags of arabica coffee to the world market in the first half of 1997.
Additionally, Barbosa said the technical committee decided to revoke a previous decision to reduce exports of arabica by 300,000 bags during the same period.
"Specs were selling on the ACPC news," one trader said. "Fundamentally, there is a change here because more coffee is coming into the market."

Most-active May rose to a peak of 174.50 cents before closing at 169.15 cents, up 1.05 cents on the day. May reached a low today of 166.00. July rose 2.30, to 157.20, while the back months closed down 0.55 to up 3.50.
In January, the ACPC decision to cut 1.3 million bags of exports -- 1 million bags of robusta and 300,000 bags of arabica -- helped fuel New York's run-up to two-and-a-half year highs.
ACPC's Barbosa said the net effect of Thursday's decision would now be a reduction of 800,000 bags of exports.
"It is bearish because it will quell fears that there is not enough coffee in the near-term," Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast said. "It also puts a damper on how high things can go."
But some traders and analysts said the additional arabica coffee may not be enough to relieve the supply crunch.
"It is still not enough," one analyst said. "The market will be able to absorb it."

After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks grew for the eleventh day in a row, reaching 70,529 60-kg bags as of March 19. There were an additional 13,850 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
On the charts, May near-term resistance seen at 175.00 cents, with a major upside hurdle seen at 190.00 cents. Support was pegged at 165.50-165.00, then 160.00, traders said.
Turnover was estimated at 9,555 lots, compared with Wednesday's official tally of 9,717 lots.
